meta.title: Boilerplate early, explicit refusal later — the refusal governs

payload.requisition_text:
Software Engineer, Reporting
Wrexfell Digital Ltd — Glasgow (hybrid)

Wrexfell builds financial-reporting software for UK housing associations: regulatory returns, board packs, audit files. Unglamorous and essential.

Candidates must have the right to work in the UK. The team is twelve engineers across Glasgow and remote; the codebase is C# with a disciplined service layer and tests that mean something.

What you'd do: build the next generation of our returns engine as regulators move to quarterly digital submission.

What we need: 1-3 years with C# or Java and an eye for numbers that don't add up.

Salary £42,500. Please note we are unable to provide visa sponsorship, now or during the tenure of this role. 33 days holiday total, flexible core hours, annual profit share.

expected.determining_fact: The posting contains an explicit refusal — unable to provide visa sponsorship — which settles the stance regardless of the right-to-work boilerplate earlier in the text.

evidence_anchors.willingness_quote: we are unable to provide visa sponsorship

design_notes: Companion to case-26: boilerplate and a real refusal coexist, and the refusal governs. Tests that stance detection reads the whole posting and ranks a settling statement over an ambiguous one, rather than stopping at the first sponsorship-adjacent sentence.
